memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For by now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with a plague that would have wiped you off the earth. But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might show you my power and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth." - Exodus 9:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two things stand together in these verses, and we must hold both.

First, mercy. God says He could have wiped Egypt out already. Every additional day Pharaoh lived was undeserved. What looked like God's weakness was actually God's restraint.

Second, purpose. God says He raised Pharaoh up so that His power would be displayed and His name proclaimed in all the earth. Paul quotes this exact verse in Romans 9:17 when discussing God's sovereignty.

This is deep water, and Christians who equally love the Bible have long differed on how it all fits together. What we can say plainly is that God is never unjust, Pharaoh was never innocent, and God's purposes are never frustrated by human rebellion.

And notice the outcome God intended: that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth. Three and a half thousand years later, we are reading about it. He accomplished exactly what He said.

The God who could overrule Pharaoh can certainly handle whatever opposes His purposes in your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I mistaken God's patience for God's inability to act?
2. How does God's sovereignty over history steady me in my own uncertainties?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, nothing escapes Your purpose. Let Your name be proclaimed through my life as well. Amen.
